infantry: Line infantry carried the smoothbore musket in close order, the backbone of every army of the 1830s.
scout: Light troops and mounted rangers went ahead of the columns to find roads, fords and the enemy.
cavalry: Lancers and dragoons gave an army its speed, its pursuit and, on open ground, its shock.
artillery: Smoothbore field guns fired roundshot and canister; they decided many battles of the period.
fleet: Sailing frigates and the first steam vessels guarded coasts and trade. Carrying armies by sea is not yet possible.
balloon: Tethered observation balloons had served France in the 1790s. Here the American armies adopt them a generation before they really did.
